rows.grounds: compound: kṛta + kṛtyaḥ; one who has fulfilled obligations
compound: guru + uttamaḥ; the supreme teacher

items.question: What state and prior actions qualify the supreme teacher to proceed with the ritual?
premises: The supreme teacher has bathed.
He has completed the twilight worship.
He has fulfilled his duties.
items.inference: Thus prepared, the supreme teacher is qualified to perform the subsequent rites.
items.plain_english: Having bathed, completed the twilight worship, and fulfilled his duties, the supreme teacher is ready.

rows.grounds: compound: bhūṣaṇa + upetaḥ; endowed with ornaments
compound: dakṣiṇā + tuṣṭa + mānasaḥ; mind satisfied by gifts

items.question: What adornments and mental disposition should characterize the supreme teacher at this stage?
premises: The teacher is endowed with fivefold ornaments.
His mind is satisfied by gifts received.
items.inference: The teacher’s external adornment and inner satisfaction mark his proper ritual condition.
uncertainties: The exact items of the fivefold adornment are not specified.
items.plain_english: He is adorned with the five ornaments and his mind is satisfied by the gifts.

rows.grounds: compound chain: daivajñaiḥ + śilpibhiḥ + toṣitaiḥ + yutaḥ; accompanied by satisfied astrologers and artisans

items.question: Which attendants must accompany the supreme teacher during the ritual proceedings?
premises: Reciters accompany the teacher.
Satisfied astrologers and artisans accompany him.
items.inference: The ritual requires the presence of duly satisfied ritual specialists and attendants.
items.plain_english: He is accompanied by reciters, and by astrologers and artisans who have been satisfied.

rows.grounds: compound: kuṇḍa + stham; standing in the fire-pit

items.question: What fire ritual actions must be performed in the prescribed sequence?
premises: The fire standing in the pit is worshipped.
The full offering is given.
These acts follow the prescribed order.
items.inference: Worship of the fire and the final offering must be completed according to the proper sequence.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped the fire in the pit and given the full offering according to the proper order,

rows.grounds: compound: prasāda + ādau; at the front of the offerings
nayet + bimbam; should lead the image
compound with sandhi marker: snāna + śvabhre + athavā; or in the bathing pit

items.question: To which locations may the ritual image be led after the fire offering?
premises: The image may be led to the front of the offerings.
Alternatively, it may be led to the bathing pit.
items.inference: The image’s placement after the fire rite allows two prescribed locations.
items.plain_english: He should lead the image to the front of the offerings, or he should lead it to the bathing pit.

rows.grounds: praṇava mantra used as seat; transliterated concept
compound: mūrti + sthāṇu; fixed in the image
describes the seat as ritually arranged

items.question: How must the ritual seat for the image be constituted and arranged?
premises: The seat is made as the praṇava.
It is arranged as fixed in the image.
items.inference: The image’s seat is ritually established through the praṇava and proper arrangement.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of mūrtisthāṇu prakalpitām is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: Having made the seat as the praṇava, arranged and fixed in the image,

rows.grounds: compound: kumbha + pānīyaiḥ; waters from pots

items.question: With what waters should the image be ritually bathed in this procedure?
premises: The image is bathed thoroughly.
The bathing uses waters from pots placed around.
items.inference: Ritual bathing requires consecrated pot waters arranged around the image.
items.plain_english: Having bathed it with waters from pots that have been placed around,

rows.grounds: compound: śiva + bhaktam; devotee of Śiva

items.question: How should the devotee of Śiva be honored after the bathing rite?
premises: Services are offered.
Other services are also offered.
The devotee of Śiva is the recipient of worship.
items.inference: The Śiva devotee must be worshipped with various ritual services.
items.plain_english: And with these and other services, one should worship the devotee of Śiva.

rows.grounds: pūjayet + naraḥ; a person should worship

items.question: What ongoing obligation follows the initial worship of the devotee?
premises: The worship begins from that time onward.
The same devotee is the object of worship.
The worship is to be performed daily.
items.inference: Daily worship of that devotee becomes a continuing duty.
items.plain_english: From then on, a person should worship that devotee daily.

rows.grounds: compound: śauca + snāna; purification and bathing
compound: sandhyā + ādi; twilight worship and so forth

items.question: Which daily observances are declared necessary alongside the ongoing worship?
premises: Purification and bathing are necessary.
Twilight worship and related acts are necessary.
Veneration is necessary.
items.inference: Daily ritual discipline includes purification, bathing, twilight rites, and veneration.
items.plain_english: Likewise, purification, bathing, twilight worship and so forth, and veneration are necessary.

rows.grounds: compound: dvāra + pārśvayoḥ; at the two sides of the door

items.question: Which principles must be worshipped at the sides of the doorway?
premises: Puruṣa is worshipped.
Prakṛti is worshipped.
The worship takes place at the sides of the door.
items.inference: The doorway worship includes honoring both Puruṣa and Prakṛti at its sides.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped Puruṣa and Prakṛti at the two sides of the door,

rows.grounds: compound: bhūta + śuddhim; purification of elements

items.question: What central worship and purification must precede the main ritual acts?
premises: The site deity is worshipped in the middle.
The purification of elements is performed.
items.inference: Central worship of Vāstu and bhūtaśuddhi are required preparatory acts.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped the site deity in the middle and having performed the purification of the elements,

rows.grounds: compound: viśeṣa + arghyam; special arghya offering
compound: kusuma + akṣata; flowers and unbroken rice
compound: toya + yuk; joined with water

items.question: What components must be prepared for the special arghya offering?
premises: A special arghya is prepared.
It is joined with flowers, unbroken rice, and water.
items.inference: The special arghya consists of flowers, unbroken rice, and water.
items.plain_english: Having prepared the special arghya, joined with flowers, unbroken rice, and water,

rows.grounds: compound: praṇava + ādyān; beginning with praṇava
compound: namaḥ + antān + mantra; mantras ending with namaḥ

items.question: What form of mantra recitation is required for ritual purification?
premises: Mantras beginning with praṇava are recited.
Mantras ending with namaḥ are recited.
The recitation is for purification.
items.inference: Purification requires reciting mantras framed by praṇava at the beginning and namaḥ at the end.
items.plain_english: One should recite mantras beginning with praṇava and ending with namaḥ for purification.

rows.grounds: compound: ṣaḍ + uttha + āsanam; the sixfold raised seat
compound: pūrva + uktena; by what was stated before

items.question: According to what procedure must the sixfold seat be established?
premises: The sixfold raised seat is made.
It follows the previously stated rule.
items.inference: The sixfold seat must be established according to the earlier prescribed procedure.
items.plain_english: Having made the sixfold raised seat according to the previously stated rule,

rows.grounds: compound: tat + tat + rūpam; that particular form
endowed or united with that form
compound: tat + tat + mūla + aṇunā; by that respective root syllable

items.question: How should the wise practitioner invoke the appropriate form using the root syllable?
premises: The wise one contemplates that particular form.
The form is endowed or united accordingly.
This is done by the respective root syllable.
items.inference: The wise practitioner unites with the appropriate form through its corresponding root syllable.
uncertainties: aṇu here likely means syllable/mantra-unit in this ritual context, not the individual self.
items.plain_english: The wise one, endowed with that particular form, should do so by means of that respective root syllable.

rows.grounds: compound: pādya + ācamanam; water for feet and sipping water
instrumental indicating use of the heart mantra

items.question: Which offerings must be presented using the heart mantra?
premises: Water for feet and sipping water are offered.
Arghya is offered.
These offerings are made with the heart mantra.
items.inference: The heart mantra is the prescribed means for offering pādya, ācamana, and arghya.
items.plain_english: One should offer water for the feet, sipping water, and arghya with the heart mantra.

rows.grounds: prefixal element in compound with dhūmakam
compound: sa + dhūmakam; together with incense

items.question: What additional offerings follow the wiping of the image with cloth?
premises: The image is wiped with a cloth.
A garment is offered.
Fragrance and incense are offered.
items.inference: After wiping, the ritual continues with offerings of garment, fragrance, and incense.
items.plain_english: Having wiped it with a cloth, one should offer a garment, fragrance, and incense.

rows.grounds: compound: tri + sandhyāsu; at the three twilight periods
dadyāt + sandhyā + dvaye + api with sandhi marker; one may also give at two twilights

items.question: At which twilight intervals may betel be offered as part of the rite?
premises: Betel is given at the three twilights.
Alternatively, it may be given at two twilights.
items.inference: The offering of betel allows either a three-twilight or two-twilight schedule.
items.plain_english: And one should give betel at the three twilights, or also at two twilights.

rows.grounds: compound: dīpa + antam; up to the lamp offering
compound: nivedya + antam; up to the food offering
yajet + śakti + anurūpataḥ; one should worship according to one’s capacity

items.question: To what extent should the worship be performed according to the worshipper’s capacity?
premises: Worship may extend up to the lamp offering.
Alternatively, it may extend up to the food offering.
The extent depends on one’s capacity.
items.inference: The scope of worship is flexible and determined by the worshipper’s capacity.
items.plain_english: One should worship up to the lamp offering or up to the food offering, according to one’s capacity.

rows.grounds: compound: prāk + uktena; by what was stated earlier

items.question: By what rule and sequence must the ritual bathing be carried out?
premises: The bathing must be done.
It follows the previously stated rule.
It follows the prescribed order.
items.inference: Ritual bathing is obligatory and must follow the earlier prescribed method and sequence.
items.plain_english: The bathing must indeed be performed according to the previously stated rule and in the prescribed order.

rows.grounds: compound: svarāḥ + ṣoḍaśa; the sixteen vowels
compound: ka + ādayaḥ; letters beginning with ka

items.question: How are the vowel and consonant groups arranged in the outer enclosures?
premises: The sixteen vowels are placed.
Outside that, the letters beginning with ka are placed.
This arrangement is considered authoritative.
items.inference: The ritual diagram places the sixteen vowels inside and the ka-group outside them.
uncertainties: The repetition tad bāhye / tad bāhye is textually present and may be emphatic or formulaic.
items.plain_english: The sixteen vowels are placed, and outside that, outside that, the letters beginning with ka are considered to be placed.

rows.grounds: compound: saṃyukta + adhamam; joined as the lowest

items.question: What is the designation of the arrangement having only one enclosure?
premises: The arrangement is joined with one enclosure.
It is designated as the lowest.
items.inference: A configuration with a single enclosure is declared to be the lowest type.
items.plain_english: Joined with one enclosure, it is declared to be the lowest.

rows.grounds: compound: janma + dine; on the birth day
compound with sandhi marker: kartuḥ + janmadine + api; also on the performer’s birth day

items.question: On which birth occasions may the prescribed observance be performed?
premises: It may be performed on the devotee’s birth day.
It may also be performed on the performer’s birth day.
items.inference: The observance is permitted on either the devotee’s or the performer’s birth day.
items.plain_english: It may be done on the devotee’s birth day, or also on the performer’s birth day.
